      Piece 3 of 24

      "U stalker"

      Our first chat on WhatsApp. I said heya, you asked how I even had your number, and within about forty seconds you had filed charges.

      It's been 577 days and you still haven't withdrawn the allegation. Fine. I plead guilty. I still recognise your typing from the three dots. I still scroll back up to old messages when I miss you. I still know the exact difference between your "okay" and your "okayy".

      Stalker, yes. But only ever yours.

      Piece 4 of 24

      Seven names for one person

      Sanu

      And the one you gave me

      Sheru. You've typed it 189 times in our chat, and every single one of them sounds different in my head. My favourite is from 4 April 2025, when I was stuck in something and you wrote "Sheruu babyuu YOU ARE BIGGER THAN THIS ❤️🧿🌹".

      You believed that before I did. I've been trying to grow into it ever since.

      Piece 5 of 24

      Stubbornly soft

      On our seven month day I wrote that you are quietly beautiful, stubbornly soft, and impossible to forget. I'd keep all of it except "quietly". Nothing about you is quiet.

      Most people meet the stubborn part first. It's the part that argues a point at 2 am, that won't drop something until it has been properly understood, that makes a decision and then defends it like a lawyer, which, to be fair, you will be. A lot of people stop there. They think that's all of you.

      Soft.

      Underneath it is the softest person I know. Scratch a little and you find her almost immediately.

      You feel things the whole way down. You remember the small thing someone said three weeks ago because it mattered to you, even if it didn't matter to them. You worry about people who would never think to worry about you. You get attached, properly attached, the kind that doesn't come with an exit plan. The stubbornness is the wall you built around something that bruises easily, and I've been lucky enough to be let inside it.

      And inside, with me, you're a different weather altogether. Clingy, playful, sleepy, silly, small. You go from arguing a case to wanting to be held in the same five minutes and you don't see any contradiction in that, because there isn't one. Strong people need holding too. Maybe more.

      I know that version of you isn't for everyone. I don't take it lightly that it's for me.

      Piece 6 of 24

      You only come in full volume

      You don't do anything at half volume. When you're happy, your whole face goes first and your voice follows. When you're hurt, it isn't a small hurt. When you love, you say it out loud, early, and you mean every word of it.

      Some people would call that too much. I think the world is far too quiet without it.

      You've sent 😭 seven thousand three hundred and thirty nine times. I've counted that as laughing, crying, and "this is so cute I'm going to die", in roughly equal parts.

      Try turning it down.

      Piece 7 of 24

      Tonight's forecast

      Your mind gets loudest when the room gets quiet. I know the pattern by now, and I want you to know I don't mind it.

      You don't overthink because you're dramatic. You overthink because you care about getting things right, and because some part of you is always checking that the people you love are still there.

      I'm still here. I'll keep saying it until your head believes it as much as your heart already does.

      In the matter of Sanya v. Shreyash

      In the High Court of Sanu

      Case No. 30/09/2002, listed for hearing every single day

      Petitioner
      Sanya, appearing in person, extremely prepared
      Respondent
      Shreyash, appearing in person, nervous
      Matter
      Who was right
      Facts
      The petitioner has decided. The respondent has presented fourteen reasons. The petitioner has decided again.
      Precedent cited
      Something the respondent said in April, quoted word for word

      Judgement

      Ruled in favour of the petitioner. Costs awarded: one hug, payable immediately.

      Decreed

      You argue like someone who already knows she'll be a professor of law. You build the case, you remember the evidence, and you don't stop until the other side concedes. It's exhausting. It's also how I know that when you're on someone's side, they're completely safe.

      And under all the legal drafting is a girl who just wants to be told she's right and then cuddled. I can do both. I've been practising.

      What you've asked for, written down

      You've told me what you need, many times and in many ways. It's never been grand gestures. It's presence. Touch. Reassurance that I'm not going anywhere. Consistency. Feeling like you're my person, and not having to ask to feel it.

      So here they are, somewhere you can come back to. Tap each one.

      Your unsaid

      Last November you wrote to me that nobody ever understood your unsaid. That you'd started to think you just hadn't found your people. And then you said I'd started to, the little things, knowing what to order for you, knowing where you'd want to sit, knowing what a nudge of your foot means.

      I've been studying since. Tap a card to see if I got it right.

      When I was interning at Dua Associates, you came and stayed with me in Delhi. For a while, life got ordinary in the best possible way. No video call to hang up, no "reached?" text, no counting days. Just you, in the same room, doing nothing in particular.

      I think about those weeks more than you'd guess. They were the trailer. I want the whole film.

      About Veer-Zaara

      It's your favourite film and it makes complete sense. It's about someone who waits, who keeps believing after everyone around her has stopped.

      You told me once that Zaara's Veer was never supposed to come back, and she kept waiting anyway. And he came.

      You love like that. Patient and stubborn at the same time. I just want to make sure you never have to wait that long for me, for anything.

      Also I have a theory about where the name Veer came from. I'm not saying it out loud.

      Nutella and bread

      Your comfort food isn't a fancy dessert or a restaurant. It's Nutella on bread. The simplest thing, done right, there whenever you need it.

      I want to be that for you. Not the big exciting thing. The thing you reach for when the day was too much, that's always in the cupboard, that never asks for anything.

      Make yourself one. Drag across the bread.

      The quiet place

      Of every place in the world, your favourite is your school, because that's where you used to find peace. Not a beach, not a city, not somewhere you went once. The place where things went quiet and you felt like yourself.

      I think about that a lot. I don't want to be the noise in your life. I want to be somewhere you find that same peace, the place you come back to after everything else.

      Sanu,

      Happy 24th birthday.

      I don't know how to write this without it turning into a list, so let me just tell you what I see when I look at you.

      I see someone who feels everything properly. Who cries at the cute thing and the sad thing and occasionally the funny thing. Who gets attached and stays attached. Who argues like she's already in court and then wants to be held like she's five. Who will be Prof. Sanya one day and will still send me a song every Friday at 12:34 am, with a note three times longer than she meant it to be.

      I know I'm not always easy to love. There have been nights that went on far too long, and things I said, or didn't say, that hurt you. I'm not going to make speeches about it here. I'm just going to keep becoming the person you saw in me before I could see him myself. Slowly, on purpose, and in ways you can actually feel.

      Thank you for choosing me, on the days it was easy and on the days it really wasn't. Thank you for Fridays. For Bubu and Sheru and every ridiculous name in between. For saying I was bigger than whatever I was stuck in, back when I didn't believe it.

      This year I want you to feel seen, heard, wanted, chosen and loved, and I never want you to have to ask for any of it.

      Here's to Kabir and Veer, to Lake Como, to the back row of your first lecture, and to every Friday still to come.

      You're not my favourite person. That's too small. You're my person.

      Yours, every day of the week,
      Sheru
